messages.content: "233 :     public static FastDateFormat getDateInstance(int style) {\n234 :         return getDateInstance(style, null, null);\n235 :     }"

The `FastDateFormat` class provides methods `getDateTimeInstance(int,int)` and `getDateInstance(int)` for creating date-time formats with date and time styles. These methods internally use the default locale when creating the date-time format objects.

Looking at the failing test `test_changeDefault_Locale_DateTimeInstance()`, it changes the default locale and then creates date-time format instances using different locales. In the test, it verifies that the locales of the created date-time formats match the locales set before creating them, as well as checks the instances are not the same object.

The current bug report indicates that the issue is related to the assumption made by `getDateTimeInstance` and `getDateInstance` methods regarding the default locale not changing. When the default locale is changed after creating the date-time format instances, the wrong locale may be applied to the format objects.

To diagnose the issue further:
1. The test changes the default locale to `Locale.US`, then creates a date-time format with `Locale.GERMANY` and another without specifying a locale (using the default locale at that point).
2. It later changes the default locale to `Locale.GERMANY` and creates another date-time format instance without specifying a locale.
3. The test then asserts that the locales of the created instances match the expected locales.
4. It also asserts that the instances are not the same, which is different behavior between versions of JUnit as indicated by the comment.

The issue is likely due to the assumption in the `getDateTimeInstance` and `getDateInstance` methods regarding the default locale not changing. When the default locale is changed after creating the formats, the wrong locale may be applied to the format objects.

To fix this issue, the `getDateTimeInstance` and `getDateInstance` methods should either update the locale of existing format instances when the default locale changes or ensure that the locale is re-evaluated dynamically when needed.

Next, I will suggest the locations to fix this issue.
```
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(int,int)
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int)
```
